name: kill drills
verdict: PASS (with a material defect found in the stop path)

sigkill.gui_reconnect: TRANSPARENT — the 98ms launchd restart fell inside the supervisor's 10s liveness-probe interval, so the GUI logged no transition at all and kept serving. Zero observed downtime at probe granularity.
sigkill.observed_transition_evidence_instead: the deliberate 88s bootout outage (V4b) produced the full connected -> offline -> connected cycle with screenshots

bootout.verdict: PASS on the requirement (stops and STAYS stopped) / DEFECT on how it stops
bootout.mechanism: launchctl bootout sends SIGTERM; the daemon's before-quit veto refuses it (runtime.daemon.quit_request_vetoed logged, shutdownAuthorized never set); launchd escalates to SIGKILL after its 'exit timeout = 5' and the process dies UNCLEANLY
bootout.note: NOT ONE daemon exit in the entire drill set produced desktop.shutdown.started / .exiting. runtimeHost.stop() never runs on any stop path; control.sock is left behind as a stale socket file.
bootout.relaunch_after_bootout: none (job unloaded, KeepAlive contract removed with it)
